title: 10 Best Self-Service BI Tools & Software In 2026
summary: Compare the 10 best self-service analytics tools in 2026, from AI analysts to warehouse-native BI, with pricing and who each tool fits best.
body_markdown:
The best self-service analytics tools in 2026 are GetDot, ThoughtSpot and Supaboard if your team wants to ask questions in plain English; Sigma, Omni and Holistics if analysts want to explore live warehouse data; and Tableau, Microsoft Power BI, Qlik Sense and Metabase if you want self-service inside an established BI platform. All of them let business users answer their own data questions without waiting on the data team. They differ in who they suit and in how the bill grows.

## How to choose a self-service analytics platform


Choose by who will use it, not by feature list: business users who won't learn a BI tool, analysts exploring warehouse data, or a team standardized on one BI vendor (the three groups below). Then put the AI layer through three tests in any trial:


- **Does it write one query, or investigate?** An assistant that turns a question into a single query and returns a chart works when the question maps onto one measure. It stops at "why", where the interpretation is still the user's job.
- **Does the number match the dashboard people already trust?** Check whether it answers through the models you already maintain (LookML, Power BI measures, dbt) or through definitions of its own.
- **Can you see how the answer was built?** Look for the SQL, any assumption it had to make, and the tables behind the answer.


The tool matters less than the rollout: shared metric definitions and a clear owner for the data models decide whether self-service sticks. Our guide to[self-service analytics](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/self-service-analytics) covers why rollouts stall and ends with a setup checklist.


## What are the best AI-native self-service analytics tools?


These tools were built around a question box rather than a dashboard: anyone types a question and gets an answer back without first learning a BI tool.


### #1: GetDot


Best for: Business users who want written answers rather than dashboards.


Full disclosure: Dot is our platform, so I'll stick to what it does. Most tools in this list make the dashboard easier to build or find, and some add a chat layer, but the output is still a chart someone has to read. Dot takes the dashboard out of the path.


#### GetDot's top features


**Answers where your team already talks.** Someone types "What was new logo revenue in EMEA last week, and how does that compare to the previous four weeks?" in Slack, Microsoft Teams, email or the web app, and Dot replies in a paragraph or two: the numbers, the trend direction, the segments that drove the change, and what likely caused them.


**A Context Agent that holds your definitions.** It reads from wherever your definitions already live (dbt models, your semantic layer, internal documentation), and every question resolves against that same set of rules. When an analyst corrects Dot ("ARR excludes free trials, not just churned accounts"), the correction becomes a proposal an admin reviews, and once it is merged, the next person to ask about ARR sees the corrected number, even on a different team.


**Investigations for "why" questions.**[Deep Analysis](https://www.getdot.ai/deep-analysis) splits a change into its drivers, tests every segment and labels the strength of the evidence behind each finding, with the SQL attached.


**Numbers that match your BI.** Looker questions run through your LookML and respect each explore's default filters, Power BI answers reuse the measures in your semantic models, and dbt and Cube definitions are read directly ([Looker](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/looker) ,[Power BI](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/power-bi) ,[dbt](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/dbt) ). Dot queries Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, and Databricks on demand, with no extracts to refresh, and every answer shows its SQL, flags any assumption it had to make, and can draw its lineage from warehouse tables to the answer.


**Reports that write themselves.** Set the metrics and the cadence, and Dot pushes a written business review to Slack, Teams, or email: a headline finding, the segments that drove the change, the likely causes, and what to do next.


Dot runs next to Tableau, Power BI, Looker, Sigma or Metabase, and when a team wants to consolidate, it can rebuild a Tableau, Power BI, Sigma or Metabase dashboard in Dot and check every chart against the original first.


#### GetDot pricing


Dot has a free plan with 300 one-time credits and full access to Pro features, so you can test it on real data before paying anything. There are three paid tiers:


- Pro: $180 per month, 150 credits included, unlimited users, $1.80 per credit overage.
- Team: $720 per month, 800 credits included, $1.44 per credit overage. Adds SSO, row-level security, embedding Dot in your app, BI migration support, and dedicated support.
- Enterprise: Custom pricing with unlimited credits, volume discounts, self-hosted deployment, audit logs, SLAs, and a dedicated account manager.


➡️ Prices above are for annual billing; month-to-month, Pro is $200 and Team is $800 a month. Credits pay for the work Dot does (query complexity and analysis depth), not the number of users, so onboarding a hundred business users doesn't multiply the bill.


#### GetDot pros and cons


✅ Business users get a written answer without learning a BI tool.


✅ One set of definitions across every team.


❌ Not a traditional dashboard tool.


❌ Credit-based pricing takes some planning for teams running very high query volumes.


➡️[Get started for free with Dot's free plan](https://app.getdot.ai/register) , or[schedule a demo](https://go.getdot.ai/meet) to see how it works with your data.


### #2: ThoughtSpot


Best for: Enterprise teams that want search-first analytics with an AI agent layered on top of governed data models.


[Source](https://www.thoughtspot.com/)


[ThoughtSpot](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/thoughtspot-alternatives) built the company on search: type a question in everyday language and get a chart from live, governed data.


#### ThoughtSpot's top features


[Source](https://www.g2.com/products/thoughtspot/reviews)


- Spotter AI agent: Runs longer investigations end-to-end, so users don't have to chain prompts together themselves.
- SpotterViz: Hand it a description, and it builds out the whole dashboard.
- ThoughtSpot Embedded: A second product line for putting search-based analytics inside your own software.


#### ThoughtSpot pricing


ThoughtSpot Analytics, for internal BI, has four tiers:


1. Essentials: From $25 per user per month (billed annually), for teams of 5-50 users, with up to 25M rows of data.
2. Pro (per user pricing): From $50 per user per month (billed annually), for 25–1,000 users, adding Spotter AI Agent (25 queries per user/month) and up to 250M rows of data.
3. Pro (usage-based): From $0.10 per query, adding Analyst Studio.
4. Enterprise (user or usage-based): Custom pricing, with unlimited users and data.


[Source](https://www.thoughtspot.com/pricing)


ThoughtSpot Embedded, for building analytics into your own application, has a Developer plan that is free for 1 year (up to 10 users and 25M rows of data) and custom-priced Enterprise plans, user-based or usage-based.


#### ThoughtSpot pros and cons


✅ Strong governance for large rollouts.


✅ Holds up on clean enterprise data models.


❌[Two pricing structures](https://www.thoughtspot.com/pricing) (per user vs. usage-based) can get confusing at scale.


### #3: Supaboard


Best for: Smaller teams and business users who want AI-built dashboards without setting up a full BI platform first.


[Source](https://supaboard.ai/)


Supaboard connects to your data sources and builds dashboards, KPIs, and reports from natural language prompts, so non-technical operators can skip the BI setup altogether.


#### Supaboard's top features


[Source](https://www.g2.com/products/supaboard/reviews#reviews)


- Chat: Ask a question, get the metric, the chart, and a written explanation back.
- Trainable AI agents: Set up agents with your own business logic and SLAs so answers stay context-aware.
- Slack and team bot integrations: Push answers and alerts into the channels your team already uses.


#### Supaboard pricing


Every plan includes a 14-day free trial:


- Individual: $83 per seat per month billed annually ($99 month to month) for a single user, default AI agent, advanced AI models, unlimited dashboards.
- Business: $208 per seat per month billed annually for multiple users, custom agents, AI embeddings, Slack integration, dedicated support.
- Enterprise: Custom pricing for unlimited users, white-labeling, dedicated account manager, and bespoke onboarding.


[Source](https://supaboard.ai/pricing)


#### Supaboard pros and cons


✅ Fast to connect data and start asking questions.


❌ It's a relatively newer entrant, so the community and integration ecosystem are still growing.


## What are the best warehouse-native self-service analytics tools?


These tools assume you already have a cloud warehouse and build exploration, modeling, and sharing directly on top of it. Looker pioneered the category, and Omni and Holistics build on its ideas with different opinions on workflow.


### #1: Sigma


Best for: Finance, ops, and analyst teams that want spreadsheet-style analytics on live warehouse data.


[Source](https://www.sigmacomputing.com/)


[Sigma](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/sigma-computing-alternatives) puts a spreadsheet interface in front of a live warehouse connection, so anyone comfortable in Excel can join tables, build pivots, and run formulas without writing SQL.


#### Sigma's top features


[Source](https://www.sigmacomputing.com/resources/library/financial-reporting)


- Warehouse-native execution: Every query runs against Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, or Databricks, so the numbers stay current.
- Ask Sigma: Natural language queries and AI-built dashboards inside the workbook.
- AI Apps: Interactive apps for forecasting, planning, and budgeting without custom development.


#### Sigma pricing


Sigma doesn't publish pricing. You'll go through a sales conversation tied to your data volume and user count.


[Source](https://www.sigmacomputing.com/company/contact-us)


#### Sigma pros and cons


✅ The spreadsheet interface is genuinely accessible.


✅ AI Apps work well for finance and ops.


❌[Pricing is custom.](https://www.sigmacomputing.com/company/contact-us)


### #2: Omni


Best for: Modern data teams that want a flexible semantic layer paired with ad-hoc workbook exploration in the same product.


[Source](https://omni.co/)


Omni was founded by ex-Looker and ex-Stitch leaders, and the influence shows: a centralized metrics model paired with workbook-style analysis, so analysts can govern while business users explore.


#### Omni's top features


[Source](https://omni.co/ai)


- Metrics-first modeling: One central definition for every metric, shared across dashboards and workbooks, no LookML required.
- AI baked into the workbook: Chart summaries, auto-generated queries, and trend explanations without leaving the canvas.
- Spreadsheet-style exploration: Live warehouse data with familiar formula syntax.
- Strong dbt integration: Bring dbt models in directly so the source of truth stays in one place.


#### Omni pricing


Omni doesn't publish pricing. You can request a free trial on their site, and they'll quote based on usage and team size.


[Source](https://omni.co/demo)


#### Omni pros and cons


✅ Flexible for both analysts and business users.


❌[No public pricing.](https://omni.co/demo)


### #3: Holistics


Best for: Engineering-led data teams that want analytics-as-code with a self-service layer for business users.


[Source](https://www.holistics.io/)


Holistics treats analytics like software: datasets and metrics are defined in declarative DSL or SQL, version-controlled in Git, and reviewed through pull requests.


#### Holistics's top features


[Source](https://www.holistics.io/as-code/)


- Centralized modeling: Joins, derived tables, and transformations defined once and reused everywhere.
- Self-service exploration: Drag-and-drop reports for non-technical users, all tied back to the governed model.
- AI-assisted queries: Natural language questions answered against the governed metrics.


#### Holistics pricing


Holistics prices by reports and users:


- Entry: $960/month, or $800/month billed annually, for 100 reports and 10 users, including hosted Git version control and dbt integration. Extra users run $15/month, and each additional 100-report block costs $120/month.
- Standard: $1,200/month, or $1,000/month billed annually, for unlimited reports and 10 users, adding custom charts, your own Git repository connection, and Google SSO.
- Security Compliance Suite: $2,400/month, or $2,000/month billed annually, adding RBAC, enterprise SSO with SAML, activity monitoring, and export controls. Extra users at $18/month.
- Custom Plan and Embedded Analytics: Custom pricing for unlimited users, advanced compliance, or white-labeled embedded dashboards.


[Source](https://www.holistics.io/pricing/?region=us)


#### Holistics pros and cons


✅ Governance scales without locking out business users.


❌[Starts from $800/month billed annually](https://www.holistics.io/pricing/?region=us) ($960 monthly), which can be expensive for SMEs.


## Self-service BI tools


Self-service BI is the dashboard-first side of[self-service analytics](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/self-service-analytics) : business users build and change their own reports in a governed BI tool instead of filing a request with the data team. Sigma, Omni and Holistics above are its warehouse-native wing. Below are the established platforms, which have added natural language search and AI assistants on top of the dashboard model, plus Domo as an all-in-one alternative.


### #1: Tableau


Best for: Visualization-led analysts and large enterprises moving toward agentic analytics through Tableau Next.


[Source](https://www.tableau.com/)


[Tableau](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/tableau-alternatives) is the visualization benchmark: its VizQL drag-and-drop engine is still what most BI tools are measured against.


#### Tableau's top features


[Source](https://www.tableau.com/products/tableau-next)


- Tableau Next: Agentic analytics through Agentforce, with semantic models and natural language at the core.
- Tableau Pulse: Sends metric updates and anomaly notes straight into Slack and email, no logging in required.
- Data Management: Central controls and reusable datasets for teams running BI at enterprise size.


#### Tableau pricing


Tableau charges per user, per month, by role. Tableau Cloud has four editions, and every deployment needs at least one Creator:


1. Tableau Standard: Creator $75, Explorer $42, and Viewer $15 per user/month, billed annually. Includes Tableau Desktop and Prep Builder for Creators, and Tableau Pulse.
2. Tableau Enterprise: Creator $115, Explorer $70, and Viewer $35 per user/month, billed annually. Adds Advanced Management and Data Management.
3. Tableau Cloud+: Custom pricing. Adds Tableau Agent across Prep, authoring, Catalog, dashboards, and Tableau Pulse, and Premier Success support.
4. Tableau+ Bundle: Custom pricing. Adds Tableau Next, Tableau Next in Slack, and Data 360.


[Source](https://www.tableau.com/pricing)


Self-hosted Tableau Server has the same Standard and Enterprise editions (Viewers from $15 and $35 per user/month, billed annually) plus a custom-priced Server+, which adds Premier Success and raises the non-production allowance from 2 environments to 6.


Tableau Next (agentic analytics) starts from $40/month/seat, with Agentforce Tableau, Tableau Semantics, and its native Slack integration; it also comes with the Tableau+ Bundle. Our[Tableau pricing guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/tableau-pricing) breaks down each edition.


#### Tableau pros and cons


✅ Still the visualization leader.


✅ Tableau Next is a real move toward agentic workflows, not a chatbot bolt-on.


❌[Per-user pricing](https://www.tableau.com/pricing) can scale fast for organizations rolling out broadly.


### #2: Microsoft Power BI


Best for: Teams already on the Microsoft stack that want self-service BI with Copilot built in.


[Source](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi)


[Power BI](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/microsoft-power-bi-alternatives) is the default BI tool for organizations on Azure, Microsoft 365, or Fabric.


#### Microsoft Power BI's top features


[Source](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi#tabs-pill-bar-ocb9d418_tab4)


- Copilot: Plain-English queries, narrative summaries, and AI-assisted report building, resolved against the underlying semantic model.
- DAX and semantic modeling: Analyst-grade dimensional modeling for teams that care about how metrics resolve.
- Row-level security: Proven at scale across enterprise deployments.


#### Microsoft Power BI pricing


- Free: Personal reports and dashboards, no sharing.
- Power BI Pro: $14/user/month, includes publishing, sharing, scheduled refresh, and Teams or SharePoint embedding.
- Power BI Premium Per User: $24/user/month, adds larger model sizes, more daily refreshes, and AI features.
- Power BI Embedded: Priced by the Azure capacity it runs on, for customer-facing analytics inside applications.


[Source](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi/pricing#tabs-pill-bar-ocbbe94_tab0)


#### Microsoft Power BI pros and cons


✅ Affordable entry point and a tight Microsoft ecosystem fit.


❌ For beginners, the learning curve can feel steep, particularly when you start working with data modeling and DAX formulas,[according to a G2 review.](https://www.g2.com/products/microsoft-microsoft-power-bi/reviews/microsoft-power-bi-review-12200381)


### #3: Qlik Sense


Best for: Regulated industries and enterprises that want associative analytics with both cloud and on-prem deployment options.


[Source](https://www.qlik.com/us/products/qlik-sense)


The associative engine is what sets Qlik Sense apart: pick any value on a chart and every other view recomputes around it on the fly, with no predefined query path.


#### Qlik Sense's top features


[Source](https://www.qlik.com/us/products/qlik-sense)


- Insight Advisor: A built-in AI layer for natural language search, automated insights, and prediction helpers.
- Real-time alerts: Watch metrics for threshold breaks and fire off automated actions when they hit.
- Flexible deployment: Cloud, on-prem, or hybrid for teams that can't move everything off their own infrastructure.


#### Qlik Sense pricing


Qlik Cloud Analytics, the SaaS version of Qlik Sense, is priced by data capacity: Starter at $300/month (10 users), Standard from $825/month (25 GB) and Premium from $2,750/month (50 GB), all billed annually ([Qlik's pricing page](https://www.qlik.com/us/pricing) ). Enterprise and client-managed Qlik Sense are quoted by sales.


[Source](https://www.qlik.com/us/products/qlik-sense)


#### Qlik Sense pros and cons


✅ Scales well on large governed datasets.


❌[One user on G2 mentions](https://www.g2.com/products/qlik-sense/reviews/qlik-sense-review-12263140) that sometimes there are loading issues, especially when business intelligence is running updates.


### #4: Metabase


Best for: Startups and lean data teams that want fast self-serve analytics with open-source roots and a flexible embedding story.


[Source](https://www.metabase.com/)


[Metabase](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/metabase-ai-alternatives) started as an open-source BI tool and still ships a free self-hosted version that goes a long way for small teams.


#### Metabase's top features


[Source](https://www.metabase.com/features/metabot-ai)


- Metabot AI: Translates everyday questions into SQL queries and charts on the fly.
- Visual query builder: A no-code path through filtering, joining, and grouping for anyone who doesn't write SQL.
- Drill-through exploration: Tap a data point on any chart to spin off a filtered view or a follow-up question.
- Embeddable everywhere: Drop dashboards into your own app with signed URLs, RLS, and SDK options.


#### Metabase pricing


1. Open Source (Self-hosted): Free, with unlimited queries, charts, and dashboards, Metabot AI with your own LLM key (since Metabase 60), and community support only.
2. Starter (Cloud-hosted): $100/month + $6/user/month, first 5 users included, adding Metabot AI through Metabase's AI service or your own AI provider key, automatic upgrades and backups, and support with a 3-day SLA.
3. Pro: $575/month + $12/user/month, first 10 users included, cloud or self-hosted, adding row- and column-level permissions, SSO and SCIM, staging + production environments, white-labeling, and embedded analytics.
4. Enterprise: Custom pricing (starts at $20k/year), adding priority support, a dedicated success engineer, and optional single-tenant or air-gapped deployment.


[Source](https://www.metabase.com/pricing/?use_case=ea)


Embedded analytics uses the same Pro and Enterprise prices, with full white-labeling, modular, SDK, or full-app embedding, and multi-tenant row- and column-level security.


#### Metabase pros and cons


✅ Free tier that's actually useful.


✅ Approachable for non-technical users.


❌ Metabot's AI usage is metered: on Metabase Cloud you either bring your own LLM key or pay per token after the first 1M, and on the free edition you bring and pay for your own key.


### Also consider: Domo


Best for: Teams that want data ingestion, dashboards, apps and AI in one platform from a single vendor.


[Source](https://www.domo.com/)


Domo wants to own the whole pipeline: connectors, data preparation, dashboards, apps and alerts, with AI chat on top. If you already load everything into a warehouse and model it in dbt, part of that bundle overlaps with what you run today.


#### Domo's top features


- Connectors: Domo's[platform page](https://www.domo.com/platform) lists 1,000+ pre-built connectors to cloud apps, databases and on-prem systems.
- Dashboards and apps: Interactive dashboards with sharing and embedding, plus custom data apps on governed data.
- AI Chat and agents: A conversational agent answers questions about company data, and an AI agent builder announced at Domopalooza in March 2026 came with a library of enterprise data connectors that work with the Model Context Protocol (MCP),[according to SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/03/25/domo-launches-ai-agent-builder-broad-enterprise-data-connectivity/) .


#### Domo pricing


As of October 2026, Domo doesn't publish a dollar price. Its pricing page offers a 30-day free trial (no credit card, the full platform, unlimited users) or custom pricing quoted by sales. Paid contracts run on consumption credits rather than seats: ingesting, storing and transforming data and using AI features draw down a credit pool. There is no permanent free tier.


[Source](https://www.domo.com/pricing)


Our[Domo pricing guide](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/domo-pricing) breaks down how credits are consumed and what third-party contract data shows.


#### Domo pros and cons


✅ Seats aren't the meter, so adding viewers doesn't add licenses.


❌ No published price, and credit consumption is harder to forecast than a seat count. We covered cheaper options in our[Domo alternatives](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/domo-ai-alternatives) breakdown.
